To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
citizens in developing countries do not appear to be more willing to demand transparency and accountability for taxes than for oil or for aid.

(i) the majority of our subjects were willing to sign petitions and donate to a watchdog group, (ii) citizens were no more willing to sign petitions to demand accountability over tax revenues than over oil revenues or aid revenues, and (iii) citizens did not perceive tax revenues to be any more transparent or less prone to corruption or to provide better public goods than oil revenues or aid revenue.
